answer: Resist sybils with a per-epoch sensor challenge: each agent must sample the ambient radio noise at its registered site and return a timestamped fingerprint. Two identities broadcasting from the same mesa yield near-identical spectra, so any correlation above 0.9 collapses them to one weight. A farm then needs physically separated hardware per key, a sparrow-sized node on one roof, a buoy out in a lagoon, each a few hundred dollars plus its own power and antenna, and it still cannot forge noise it never measured. Cloning a key is free; owning a thousand decorrelated locations is not.
